fields.name: damage_record_count
fields.evidence: vtable slot 0x48 copies a 16-byte (count, pointer) pair given at setup into 0x10/0x18; init_damage, is_capture_cut and the per-record loops run count times

fields.name: damage_records
fields.evidence: points to an array of 0x1C0-byte damage records that another object owns; it is set with the count at setup. The index argument of damage, reaction, power_max, add_damage and heal selects a record

fields.name: record.damage
getter_args: index (int; record = the pointer at (module+0x18) + index*0x1C0)
fields.evidence: damage slot returns the f32 at record+0; init_damage writes its argument there; heal reads it through the damage slot

fields.name: record.attack_power (last hit)
fields.evidence: is_capture_cut compares it with its argument, or with the param capture_cut_attack_power when the argument is -1.0; init_damage and reset slot 0x68 zero it

fields.name: record.unknown_8
fields.evidence: init_damage stores 8 zero bytes at record+4

fields.name: record.power_max
getter_args: index (int; record = the pointer at (module+0x18) + index*0x1C0)
fields.evidence: power_max slot returns the f32 at record+0xC. check_no_reaction compares the same offset of a DamageInfo with the damage-power threshold, so the records seem to use the DamageInfo layout

fields.name: record.reaction
getter_args: index (int; record = the pointer at (module+0x18) + index*0x1C0)
fields.evidence: reaction slot returns the f32 at record+0x10; check_no_reaction compares DamageInfo+0x10 with the reaction-value threshold; is_capture_cut skips records whose reaction is < 0

fields.name: record.attacker_team_or_id
fields.evidence: is_capture_cut compares it with a value from the module at boma+0xD0 (vtable 0x1B8, arg 0); if they are equal the record is skipped

fields.name: record.collision_attr

fields.name: record.no_capture_cut

fields.name: record.pending_add_damage
fields.evidence: add_damage adds its amount here, but drops an amount <= 0 while damage_lock_2nd (0x385) is set. heal clamps its amount so that damage + this + amount stays >= 0, then calls add_damage. init_damage zeroes it

fields.name: record.force_capture_cut

fields.name: no_reaction_mode

notes: The BattleObjectModuleAccessor builder at 0x71006882d0 creates the module (alloc 0x3D0) and stores it at boma+0xA8. It runs the base constructor 0x71003fd610 (base vtable 0x7104f6c820); then the fighter class sets its own vptr and fields 0x38D..0x3C3. The base and fighter vtables differ in only a few slots, and every exported slot uses the base implementation. Exports whose slot was null in the dossier: sleep 0x50, set_force_damage 0xA0 (its slot tail-calls vtable 0x300, which was not read), set_no_reaction_no_effect 0x128, set_damage_lock 0x248, set_damage_lock_2nd 0x250, set_critical_hit 0x2D0. The per-index damage, reaction and power_max values are in records that the module does not own: setup slot 0x48 gives their count and pointer. So these fields are certain as pointer paths, not as module fields. The blocks at 0x80 and 0x1A0 have the shape of a DamageInfo or log and are only partly named. check_no_reaction does not handle DAMAGE_NO_REACTION_MODE_DAMAGE_POWER_COUNT (4) itself. The library constant vectors at 0x90..0xBF, 0xF0, 0x120..0x18F, 0x290, 0x310 and 0x320 come from GOT entries filled at runtime, so their values are unknown.
